Plot_Notes: PIBA dominant in stand with some PIAL, aspen, and PICO nearby. 10+ PIBA saplings show significant flagging on South side of tree. D-side + = uphill, D-side - = downhill. No veg line survey completed for this plot.

Large avalanche effect, huge MECH damage, most trees experience needle minor. No sapling count for this plot. Clump 1 has 3 additional dead stems and 1 live small stem. Clump 6 has 1 additional dead + 2 live fallen stems. Clump 7 has 2 additional dead stems broken at base and 1 live branch/stem. Clump 10 has 11 additional stems, 0-5.7 DBH and 0.3-3m tall.

Plot_Route: Whitney Portal to Guitar Lake, then camped by confluence of creeks. Plot west of Camp ~0.8 miles.
Plot_Notes: No target species (PIMO) found on the way to or in the plot. Could be 1 PIMO across the Kern River. PIBA dominant, but decided to do PICO due to lack of extreme dry PICO plots and several options of PIBA near here.

Plot_Route: Whitney Portal, camped West of lower Crabtree meadows, hiked to the end of 0.8 mile trail and contoured the plot.
Plot_Notes: Dominant species is PICO with occasional sparse PIBA. Cored all PIBA and paired PICO + took needles. Measured all trees. PICO dominant. Used randomly selected point, but chose direction to capture sparse PIBA. Could have extended length to get a few more PIBA, but not while measuring all trees. Too steep to extend width much. Used GPS for position due to one hypso. HTL= height to live.

Plot_Route: Whitney Portal, North to Confluence camp then off trail to edge of Plateau.
Plot_Notes: No PIBA at point and sparse in area, so did a PICO plot. Point randomly selected, direction randomly selected (1 vs. 2 on app). Most trees experiencing suppression. Seasonal dry drainage near plot center.  Dside+ = uphill/right. Most low % live values are due to suppression.

Plot_Route: From lower Crabtree camp, took JMT for ~1.5 miles, then off trail for 1.5 miles.
Plot_Notes: No PIMO for miles. Most of this South-facing slope is PICO dominant, but the plot is on a ledge just before the drop into the Kern, so species diversity is high due to abrupt elevation change. Shorter downslope transect belt (10m versus 28m upslope) due to steepening slope >35 degrees past the ledge. A few single trees + clusters of ~10 PICO with beetles near plot on the way in, but restricted to clusters- does tree diversity or climate keep beetles in check? No alternate hosts in plot, but lots of pedicularis semibarbata on the way to the plot, esp. on ridge above plot. Lots of big scars on both PIBA + PICO, probably lightning. Ips and western gal rust probably in plot.

Plot_Route: Lakes trail, wolverton, lonely lake
Plot_Notes: no PIAL in designated plot, shifted ~65 m cross-slope to nearest PIAL stand, sparse at beginning of transect and becomes more dense closer to 50m, full sun, consistent clouds 2-4pm and no direct shade, snow on nearby peaks, plot took two days to complete

Plot_Route: Mitchell Peak, Jennie Lakes Trailhead to Sugarloaf, 800m off trail
Plot_Notes: Plot shifted ~131m to nearest PICO stand, downslope from original plot. High % overall dead mostly due to suppression. Really dense PICO regen in former meadow, just downslope/SE from plot- likely post-high severity fire in this patch. One additional PICO <1.37m.

Plot_Route: Jennie Lakes Trailhead to Sugarloaf then off trail ~450m
Plot_Notes: Some dense patches of ABMA and PICO regen in places that may have been high severity fire. ABMA is dominant. No PICO at random point shifted to nearest SE (ish) stand. PICO is (80m) pretty sparse in this area except a small NE facing stand. Substantial 1000h fuels in addition to 1s, 10s, 100s.

Plot_Route: Jennie Lakes Trailhead to Sugarloaf
Plot_Notes: No PILA for at least 150m, small group of PILA or PIJE on ridge between here and Sugarloaf, check strara for PICO (likely below 7), flat and sandy, lots of PIJE cones (reproducing well), nice views, closest tree to creek ~65m, evidence of recent fire as being patchy, due to limited fuels, sparse vegetation, random selecting for EMF trees, #1-41 then reject PIJE, <15cm DBH, and needles too high or repeat, tree #17 beetle tree

Plot_Route: Jennie Lakes Trailhead to Sugarloaf
Plot_Notes: No PICO at immediate point. Terrain rolly, shifted to most South possibility which is ~SW. Plot start is ~21m from trail but ~2 trees are closer (PIMOS) and other trees much farther. Plot start not randomized due to double plot challenges, but closest South stand. No evidence of fire scars, patchy beelte kill throughout plot. Double plot with PIMO, share veg datasheet and plot notes.

Plot_Route: Jennie Lakes Trailhead to Sugarloaf

Plot start not randomized due to double plot challenges, but closest South stand. No evidence of fire scars, patchy beelte kill throughout plot. Double plot with PICO, share veg datasheet and plot notes.

Plot_Route: Twin Lakes Trailhead
Plot_Notes: No target species found, just ABMA. No recent fire, large fuel load of all size classes throughout plot. One PICO. At least one jeffrey clump with 3 stems ~ 30, 25, 20 DBH. Tallest PIJE is 13m. Trees measured are similar in slope, elevation and aspect, but scattered throughout area. Trees 1 and 2 were cored, but no data collected.

Plot_Route: Crown Valley "Trail" to Tehipite "Trail"
Associated_Tree_Species: PIJE, ABCO, QUKE, CADE, Pinon Pine
Plot_Notes: Lots of seedling and sapling recruitment, but only 1 cone on a tree and 1 large mature cone on the ground. Some larger PILA within 100-1000m may be within dispersal distance. Rockfall from cliffs above appears to have knocked down trees of all species including PILA. Open space may be good for regen. WPBR seems high- check BRS plot 68 and nearby plot for older trends.

Plot_Route: Crown Valley "Trail" to Tehipite "Trail"/ Theodore Solomon "Trail"
Plot_Notes: Unripe PILA cones on groung throughout plot-- chewed off tree or blown by wind? Most PILA in plot have no cones or yr 1 cones. A few large trees across the river and on the negative side of the transect have more mature cones. Plot shifted from rock outcrop ~187m  due to no PILA. Only PIJE and Pinon pine at random point. Shifted to nearest stand. Closest trees to river still ~50m away from water, but closer to sandy wash that may occasionally flood (conifers >5-10 years old growing on it). Some old charred logs- long time since fire.

Plot_Route: Cross Kings river from campsite at Simpson Meadow Junction, then ascend trail ~ 2 miles
Plot_Notes: Open, sparse, PIJE are dominant species and CADE dominant regen. Long time since last fire- some bole char on very big trees and old charred CADE stumps + 1 CADE. Windy lightning fire was just above plot earlier this summer- can see singed trees. ~100m from tree 1 to river, but ~40m from satellite tree #6. No PILA at 2b or 2c. Found only 2 PILA uphill from 2c ~200m, 1 too close to river and upslope, bad aspect and acessibility issues. 2 other trees too close to trail. Shifted to nearest stand 3+ trees between.... (paper tore, no remaining notes).

Plot_Route: Hiked from Shake Camp to Summit Lake then contoured around the side of Sheep Mountain from Summit Lake.
Plot_Notes: No associated trees higher up (likely near the high end of the local range for ABMA and PIMO). Granite talus field dominates the middle of the plot, so low percent cover, but high understory species diversity.

Plot_Route: From Shake Camp follow trail to Summit Lake. Plot is about 100m above the lake on the north side.
Plot_Notes: PICO is dominant, no foxtail in plot (supposed to be a PIBA8 or maybe PIBA6 and PIMO6), several PIBA on Sheep Mountain Ridge to the east and one at lake level near the outlet (N facing). Historic(?) can at the 50m end.

Plot_Route: From Shake Camp follow trail to Summit Lake. Plot is about 100m above the lake on the north side.
Plot_Notes: Trees 1-3 have a slope of 1-2 degrees, aspect 180 degrees, about 20-30m from Summit Lake next to camp and the (largely unmaintained) trail. Trees 4-9 are in the PIMO6 plot or immediately adjacent to the plot. Trees 10 and 11 are between plot and camp. No needles collected in this plot because the leaf-c was broken. Most would be collectable with the leaf-c but not without. One was too high for the leaf-c.

Plot_Route: Contour around the benches from lower Lamark Lakes
Plot_Notes: Beautiful!

Plot_Route: Take the Bishop Pass trail to the junction with the JMT. Can camp near the junction and plot is just north.
Plot_Notes: PICO is dominant, but there are PIMO (the target species). Close to the JMT. Shifted slightly more than 200m north of the original plot since there were no PIMO at the original point. Several broken PICO in the middle of the plot probably due to avalance or rockfall. PICO is dominant in this area with red fir sprinkled in. PIMO is fairly sparse, especially on south-facing slopes with more on north aspects. HTL = height to live needles. Lots of aspen at the 100m end, but did not assess for prisms--many stems! About 20% cover for POTR. 100m very open with 1 live PIMO. 2 PIMO ~ 147m upslope around 70m out. More (~10-12) further up the JMT, but the shift would be way over 500m and to a higher elevation. Some larger PIMO across the canyon N and E facing and we saw a few W facing on the way down Bishop Pass trail to the JMT--just hard to find south-facing PIMO in this area. Clump of PIAL about -10m dSIDE, 86.5m dOUT, 3 live stems, 1 below DBH, 1 about 4m tall, 6 DBH with a dead toop and 40% dead, the other about 3m tall, 4cm DBH with 20% dead.

Plot_Route: Climb off trail from the drainage before Buck Creek Bridge and bushwack/create a trail through dense manzanita and other shrubs
Plot_Notes: Approach was horrific--we attempted walking up the creek, but hit waterfalls. We bushwacked and sawed our way through manzanita, and eventually discovered a coute up a drainage with a relatively short bushwhack. JEC scouted original point to within 30m, and found 2 live and 1 dead PILA. However, this point was way too far from our camp at Buck Creek as it took the whole day to get there given the dense shrub cover. Although the site had PILA, it was not feasible to read a plot and travel there from the nearest possible campsite in a single day. Too far and PILA was similarly sparse. Shifted the plot to the saddle (flat with some trees on the East and West side of the saddle) and satelite grove (more similar east aspect like the original point) to keep the day trips from Buck Creek humanly possible. 5 PILA seedlings in the full plot, more PIJE and many more CADE and ABCO seedlings and saplings too, but no formal count due to the large/balloon nature of the plot and time constraints with only 2 people. Lots of PILA regen (seedlings and saplings) near the satelite clump plus a few in between the main transect and the satelite portion of the plot. Only one of these was measured to check if it was coreable (14 DBH). No fire scar on trees, but area has lots of dead and down, including some PILA on the saddle. Evidence of charred stumps and burned logs, so perhaps an older fire than expected based on the imagery that suggested a fire in 2021 or the fire was really patchy.

Plot_Route: Parked at house near Redwood Saddle and walked down the road to the bend then took cow trails to a little creek
Other_Associated_Species: PTAQ, SARA, Erythranthe guttata in riparian areas
Plot_Notes: Plot burned in Castle Fire (2021), low severity near this little creek. Only a few trees burned by the creek. Overall region seems to be more mixed severity. For Prisms data QUKE and 2/4 QUCH, the main stem is dead, but resprouting

Plot_Route: Parked at a wide spot on the road to Redwood Saddle and climbed down the road cut to the plot.
Plot_Notes: The original point was only 40m from the USFS dirt road to Redwood Saddle. Plot would have had 2-3 live PILA, 1 sapling, and 1 dead PILA. The shift puts plot more than 50m from the road and captures 7 live PILA. Added 2 live and 1 dead PILA from the original point on the way back to the car. 1 healthy PILA in the negative dOut direction about 50m to the side, 2 healthy PILA about 90m farther to the side and downslope from tree #5. One fire or beetle killed PILA about 110m farther out and to the side + 1 healthy PILA 164m farther out and farther to the side. This may be an EMF cold vs. dry comparison plot--check with Anna.

Plot_Route: Park at Lost Grove restrooms and plot is just downslope in the sequoia grove.
Plot_Notes: Original point was less than 50m from General's Highway. Shifted point downslope to increase distance from the highway and to capture more PILA. Extending the transect beyond 50m would capture 4+ dead PILA in 50-100m then 2+ live PILA and 5+ dead PILA in 100-200m. However, these trees are close to the road and buildings (some are also marked as hazard trees with blue paint). This could be done as a separate transect, especially if rounds from the marked trees could be collected after they are cut. Point selection for the 11 trees in this plot was based on maximizing live PILA.

Plot_Route: Off trail from NPS access road at Cabin Creek
Plot_Notes: Slope at the 50m is 10 degrees, but this should be consistent with the overall average of the 0m and the 150 end.

Plot_Route: Just off Twin Lakes Trail, just above Silliman Creek
Other_Associated_Species: CHSE, PTAQ, PYPI, PYAS, MOOD, ARPA
Plot_Notes: 2022 notes: One seedling near tree 1, at tree 5 overall aspect (i.e. direction of streamflow was 182), but the local aspect was 112 since water would flow pas the tree into the south-flowing stream. One additional large PILA visible 109m downstream from tree 5. 2024 notes: Ribes nevadense and Ribes roezlii in plot, PILA seedlings near tree #7 (dead snag). Many ABCO seedlings and saplings.

Plot_Route: 250m off Giant Forest local trail towards the Wolverton/High Sierra Trail cutoff
Plot_Notes: revisit of 2022 plot. 2022 notes: ABCO is dominant and plot is quite open due to fire. No sugar pines visible for the next 50-100m cross slope. The nearest PILA to the side is 87m upslope on a ridge with a different aspect. Nearest downslope PILAs are over 100m away at a different elevation. No needles collected since all were too high except tree 4, which was singed by fire.

Plot_Route: Park near Crescent Meadow, hike to Tharp's Log and head upslope past the NPS recording equipment and USGS demography ABCO plot
Plot_Notes: revist of 2022 plot. 2022 notes: point 399 (no averaging) is the original point with multiple hazard trees. point 400 is the shifted point. Other trees in the area were too scortched (greater than 10% or had wpbr). No needles within reach except tree 5 (singed) and tree 2. Plot is within the 2021 Huckleberry Rx burn and the trail was the fire break. There is more WPBR outside the Rx burn area.

Plot_Route: Off-trail from ~0.5 miles up Twin Lakes Trailhead
Plot_Notes: Rejected PIMO plot but collected veg data. Plot/veg notes: Mixed forest with PICO, PIJE, ABMA, 1 JUOC sapling. Most herbaceous species have gone to seed and are dried. Several downed trees in plot. Significant fire scars ~5m high on some PIJE. Forest --> Shrubland just upslope, indicated by large amounts of manzanita. Post fire regen evident, many ABMA saplings in/just below plot. Veg survey took ~ 2 hours.
